user_story: As a user I start the desktop app and get a native window.
expected: A window titled 'Joplin Lite' opens at 1400x900, resizable, minimum 1024x640.
evidence: real session: window titled 'Joplin Lite' at 1400x900 (frame 1400x891); an AppleScript resize to 700x400 clamps to the 1024x640 minimum (title fixed in web/src/routes/__root.tsx)
fix: web/src/routes/__root.tsx: document.title is now 'Joplin Lite', which the system webview adopts as the native window title (it was 'joplin-lite'). Geometry and the 1024x640 minimum were verified on a real session.

user_story: As a user I can open my vault without running a Node server, in the native app or through the served web build.
expected: `gojoplin serve --web-dir <dist>` serves index.html and hashed assets from internal/webui; the desktop app renders the workspace natively, with no Node server and no browser engine.
fix: The embedded SPA left the desktop shell in the native-ui migration: the workspace is a native window and the web build is served by `gojoplin serve --web-dir` through internal/webui. The handler's tests moved with it (TestInjectsRuntimeConfig, TestSPAFallbackAndAssets), so SH-02/03/13 are re-pointed at internal/webui.

user_story: As the page I receive API coordinates before the bundle runs.
expected: window.__GOJOPLIN__ = {base, token, shell, profile} is injected before </head>, JSON-escaped so the payload cannot close the tag.
fix: Same move: runtime config injection is internal/webui's job now, covered by TestInjectsRuntimeConfig and TestEscapesScriptBreakout.

user_story: As a user I get one program with one lifecycle.
expected: The clipper/Data API binds before the window opens; no separate process or Node runtime.
fix: Added shell/backend_test.go: the in-process API is started and probed headlessly (no webview).

user_story: As a user without a configured api.token I still get a working UI.
expected: A random 48-hex token is minted per session, never persisted, and never logged; a warning is logged.
fix: Same test: a 48-hex ephemeral token is minted when none is configured, is not persisted, and a configured token is reused verbatim.

user_story: As a user a second launch focuses the running app.
expected: The second process exits and shows/focuses the existing window instead of opening another.
evidence: real session: a second launch exits 0 immediately while the first keeps serving its port and window (RequestSingleInstanceLock)

user_story: As a user my window size and position are remembered.
expected: MyGO restores the window geometry for StateKey 'main' on the next launch.
evidence: real session: MyGO restores 'main' from window-state.json under PathUserData; a seeded 1180x760 produced a 2360px-wide smoke capture and a resized 1024x640 survived quit/relaunch

user_story: As a user closing the window shuts everything down.
expected: Closing the window stops the HTTP server and closes SQLite; Close is idempotent.
fix: Same test: Close() stops the server and is idempotent.

user_story: As a user I am told when the API cannot start.
expected: A native error dialog names the bind failure and points at port 41184; the app then quits.
evidence: real session: with 41184 held, startup logs 'cannot start the local API on localhost:41184 ... bind: address already in use ... Joplin desktop uses port 41184' and blocks on the native dialog until dismissed, then quits

user_story: As a user I decide whether a browser extension may pair.
expected: A native Accept/Reject dialog appears; Reject is the default and no prompt means no grant.
evidence: real session: POST /auth opens the native pairing dialog, /auth/check reports waiting, and Return (the default button) rejects and returns no token

user_story: As a user the app shows its own icon in the dock.
expected: The embedded PNG is applied via Dock.SetIcon; failures are logged, not fatal.
evidence: real session: shell/bundle.sh builds 'tmp/Joplin Lite.app' (com.joplinlite.desktop, app-icon.icns); the app still applies the embedded 512px PNG with Dock.SetIcon and -smoke reports icon: 'ok' (no 'cannot set application icon' warning)
fix: Added shell/bundle.sh: a macOS 'tmp/Joplin Lite.app' (CFBundleIdentifier com.joplinlite.desktop + app-icon.icns). The runtime path is unchanged and verified: the shell reads android-chrome-512x512.png from the embedded bundle, calls Dock.SetIcon with it, logs a failure if any, and -smoke now records the result ('icon': 'ok').

user_story: As a developer I can verify the real webview in CI.
expected: -smoke evaluates the live page, calls the API (GET + POST/DELETE), writes tmp/desktop-smoke.{json,png}, then quits.
evidence: real session: -smoke evaluates the live page, GET + POST/DELETE the in-process API, writes tmp/desktop-smoke.{json,png}, then quits

user_story: As a user deep links work and assets are cached correctly.
expected: Extensionless paths serve index.html with no-cache; /assets/* are immutable; missing assets 404; writes are rejected.
fix: Same move: SPA fallback, asset caching and write rejection are covered by TestSPAFallbackAndAssets and TestRejectsWrites in internal/webui.

user_story: As a user I can run local-only.
expected: -no-sync serves and edits the local database with no remote, no sync loop, and no lock work.
fix: Same test: no-sync serve starts without a remote.

user_story: As a user I can move the local API off 41184.
expected: -addr <host:port> overrides server.port/listen_host and the page's injected base follows it.
fix: Same test: the -addr override is the address that actually serves.

user_story: As a user I can point the app at another database.
expected: -data-dir overrides server.data_dir; the profile key (recovery namespace) follows the resolved path.
fix: Same test: the -data-dir override is opened and drives the profile key.

user_story: As a user I open the workspace and see my library.
expected: Notebooks, tags and the newest 50 note summaries load; footer says 'Saved locally'; no synthetic data appears.

user_story: As a new user with no notes I get a clear first step.
expected: The list shows 'Your library is ready for its first note' with a Create button that starts a note.

user_story: As a user I press New note and start writing.
expected: A note titled 'Untitled note' is created through the API, appears first, is selected, and its body is editable.

user_story: As a user I create a note while a notebook is selected.
expected: The new note is created in that notebook (parent_id), which stays selected in the sidebar.
evidence: qa/test_ui.mjs — create note in selected notebook

user_story: As a user I create a note while a tag filter is active.
expected: The tag filter clears, the new note is selected, and the list returns to the unfiltered notebook scope.

user_story: As a user my typing is saved without a Save button.
expected: Body edits save after ~600 ms; the footer shows Saving locally… then Saved locally; the stored body matches.

user_story: As a user I can reload immediately after typing and keep my text.
expected: Pending edits are journaled synchronously to localStorage and flushed on load, so an instant reload loses nothing.

user_story: As a user I rename a note.
expected: Manage note exposes a required title field; saving updates the header, the list row and the API.
evidence: qa/test_ui.mjs — title edit via Manage note

user_story: As a user I move a note between notebooks.
expected: Manage note's Notebook select updates parent_id; notebook name and counts update after save.

user_story: As a user I attach an existing tag.
expected: Manage note checkboxes attach the tag; the chip appears in the header and beside the list row.

user_story: As a user I create a tag while organizing a note.
expected: New tag is created (reusing an existing title case-insensitively), attached, and shown in the sidebar.

user_story: As a user I detach a tag from a note.
expected: Unchecking and saving removes the association; the chip disappears and the API no longer lists it.

user_story: As a user I delete a note deliberately.
expected: Delete note asks for confirmation, 'Delete permanently' removes it, the row disappears and GET returns 404.

user_story: As a user I can back out of deleting.
expected: 'Keep note' closes the confirmation and leaves the note and its body untouched.

user_story: As a user I can discard unsubmitted details.
expected: Cancel closes Manage note without changing title, notebook or tags.

user_story: As a user I complete a to-do note.
expected: The toggle writes todo_completed, updates the header state and the list icon color without losing the body.

user_story: As a user I see when an open to-do is due.
expected: An incomplete to-do with todo_due shows '· due <date>' in the list; completed ones do not.

user_story: As a user I can preview a note.
expected: Preview renders headings, emphasis, lists, code blocks and links from the Markdown source.

user_story: As a user a malicious note cannot run script.
expected: Raw HTML is not rendered; script/img handlers are removed by DOMPurify while plain Markdown still renders.

user_story: As a user I see task checkboxes in preview.
expected: '- [ ]' and '- [x]' list items render as disabled, labelled checkboxes; other brackets stay text.

user_story: As a user I am told when both sides changed a note.
expected: A conflict note shows the 'nothing was overwritten' banner with the kept-copy explanation.

user_story: As a user I can act on a conflict from the banner.
expected: 'Open synced version' navigates to the synced original; 'Keep my copy' dismisses the banner. No dead controls.

user_story: As a user I find a note by its title.
expected: Typing part of a title lists matching notes and the list header names the query.
fix: search/tags/query list endpoints now honor include_conflicts and api.ts sends it, so conflict notes are findable from search and scoped lists.

user_story: As a user I find a note by words in its body.
expected: Body-only terms match through the FTS index, case-insensitively.

user_story: As a user search does not fire per keystroke.
expected: A 250 ms pause produces one /search request for the accumulated query.

user_story: As a user I understand an empty search.
expected: The list says 'No notes match “q”' and offers Clear search, which restores the library.

user_story: As a user Esc clears search quickly.
expected: Escape empties the query and restores the unfiltered list (except while a dialog is open).

user_story: As a user Cmd/Ctrl+K jumps to search.
expected: The keyboard shortcut focuses the search field and prevents the browser's own binding.

user_story: As a user I scope the list to a notebook.
expected: Selecting a notebook lists only its notes, titles the list with the notebook, and marks it current.

user_story: As a user I navigate arbitrarily deep notebook trees.
expected: Every level renders indented with a guide line; a note in a third-level notebook is reachable by clicking it.

user_story: As a user I add a top-level notebook.
expected: New notebook creates it with no parent, closes the form, and shows it in the sidebar.

user_story: As a user I nest a new notebook.
expected: Choosing a parent in the form creates the notebook under it and it renders at the next level.

user_story: As a user I see how many notes each notebook holds.
expected: With the full library loaded, each notebook shows its exact note count (descendants included).
evidence: qa/test_ui.mjs — exact notebook counts when whole library loaded
fix: vault.tsx sets countsExact(true) once the whole library is loaded, re-enabling sidebar counts.

user_story: As a user I am not shown a wrong total.
expected: When only a page is loaded, per-notebook/tag counts are omitted and All notes shows '+' instead of a false total.
evidence: qa/test_ui.mjs — paged counts are not fake totals

user_story: As a user I scope the list to a tag.
expected: Selecting a tag lists only tagged notes and titles the list 'Tag: <name>'.

user_story: As a user I see tag note counts when they are trustworthy.
expected: Counts match the loaded full library; they are hidden on a paginated partial load.

user_story: As a user I can page past the first 50 notes.
expected: Load more appends the next keyset page with no duplicate rows and hides at the end.

user_story: As a user I move through the list without the mouse.
expected: Up/Down/Home/End move focus (not selection), clamped at the ends; Tab leaves the list; Enter opens the focused note.

user_story: As a user opening a note loads its full body.
expected: The list ships summaries only; selecting a row issues GET /notes/{id} and the editor shows that body.

user_story: As a user I can judge a note from its row.
expected: Rows show title, excerpt, notebook, tags, updated time, and an amber due date for open to-dos.

user_story: As a user excerpts are readable.
expected: The first non-empty line has leading Markdown markers stripped, whitespace collapsed and is capped at 140 runes.

user_story: As a user I can explicitly refresh from disk.
expected: Reload shows a busy state, flushes pending saves, and refetches metadata, the current page and the open note.

user_story: As a user I always know whether my work is stored.
expected: Footer states are Saved locally / Saving locally… / Local save failed, reflecting the real write state.

user_story: As a user I never mistake a failed backend for demo data.
expected: When the API is unreachable the app shows an error/retry state, disables editing, and does not substitute mock notes.

user_story: As a user Retry restores the workspace.
expected: Retry reconnects, reloads metadata and the list, and re-enables editing without a page reload.

user_story: As a user a failed save is visible and recoverable.
expected: A failed write surfaces an alert and the failed footer state; the text stays in the editor and a retry can persist it.

user_story: As a phone-width user I get one pane at a time.
expected: Below 1024 px the list and editor swap, Navigation opens as a dialog, and Back returns to the list.

user_story: As a laptop user I keep all three panes.
expected: At 1024x640 the sidebar, list and editor are all visible and the page does not scroll horizontally.

user_story: As a user I choose light, dark or system.
expected: The choice persists across reloads and immediately changes the rendered theme.

user_story: As a user on 'System' the app follows OS changes.
expected: A prefers-color-scheme change re-applies the theme while the explicit choice still overrides it.

user_story: As a user I can see what the app is doing locally.
expected: Settings identifies Local workspace, explains that sync/E2EE are configured outside the UI, and closes with Escape.

user_story: As a keyboard/screen-reader user every control is usable.
expected: Icon-only buttons have names, controls are >=44 px touch targets where space allows, and focus returns after dialogs.

user_story: As a user long titles and bodies do not break the layout.
expected: Long titles/excerpts truncate with ellipsis and the document has no horizontal overflow at 390/1024/1440 px.

user_story: As a user I see where the open note lives.
expected: The editor header shows notebook, updated time and one chip per tag.

user_story: As a user deleting the open note selects something sensible.
expected: The next row becomes active, or the editor shows the empty state when none remain.
evidence: qa/test_ui.mjs — delete selects the next note

user_story: As a user a reload keeps my place.
expected: If the open note still exists after Reload, it stays selected and its body is refreshed.

user_story: As a user I can clear a tag filter by clicking it again.
expected: Clicking the active tag deselects it and returns to All notes.

user_story: As a user I cannot create a nameless notebook.
expected: The Create notebook button stays disabled for an empty/whitespace title; Escape/Cancel abandons the form.

user_story: As a user I do not get duplicate tags from case differences.
expected: A new tag whose title matches an existing tag case-insensitively reuses that tag.

user_story: As a user API errors are readable.
expected: Errors are shown as 'METHOD /path → status: message', not a raw stack or silent failure.

user_story: As a user an edit made while the API blips is not lost.
expected: The journaled edit is retried on the browser 'online' event and on the next save/reload.
evidence: qa/test_ui.mjs — offline recovery retries the journaled edit

user_story: As a user the workspace loads without errors.
expected: First load produces no uncaught page errors, unhandled rejections, or hydration warnings.

user_story: As a Joplin client I can discover the clipper.
expected: GET /ping returns text/plain 'JoplinClipperServer' with 200, unauthenticated.

user_story: As an operator I can probe liveness.
expected: GET /health returns 200 with no body and no auth.
evidence: qa/test_api.py — health is open and empty

user_story: As a user my data is not readable without the token.
expected: Any non-open route without ?token= or Bearer returns 403 with a JSON error.

user_story: As a user a wrong token is rejected.
expected: ?token=wrong returns 403 'Invalid "token" parameter'.

user_story: As CLI tooling I can use a bearer key.
expected: Authorization: Bearer <api.key or api.token> is accepted on protected routes.

user_story: As the web clipper I start pairing.
expected: POST /auth from a non-web origin returns {'auth_token': <32 hex>} and status becomes waiting.

user_story: As the extension I poll pairing state.
expected: GET /auth/check?auth_token=<x> returns {'status':'waiting'} until a decision exists.

user_story: As a user I approve pairing.
expected: Accepting resolves the request and /auth/check returns accepted plus the API token.

user_story: As a user I refuse pairing.
expected: Rejecting resolves it to rejected and no token is ever returned.
evidence: qa/test_api.py — pairing reject never yields the token

user_story: As a user a web page cannot pair itself.
expected: POST /auth and /auth/check from an http(s) Origin return 403; extension/native origins are allowed.

user_story: As the extension I can verify a stored token.
expected: GET /auth/check?token=<x> returns {'valid': true|false}; without params it is 400 'Invalid request'.

user_story: As a client I list notes newest first.
expected: GET /notes returns up to 10 full notes with has_more, ordered by updated_time desc.

evidence: qa/test_api.py — pagination is capped and offset

user_story: As a client I can request only some fields.
expected: fields=id,title returns objects with exactly those keys, for lists and single items.

user_story: As a client I can order by an allowed column.
expected: order_by=title&order_dir=asc sorts by title; unknown columns fall back to updated_time and unknown dirs to DESC.

user_story: As the webview I fetch rows without bodies.
expected: summary=1 returns excerpt (<=140 runes), tag_ids and no body field.
fix: store/summaries.go: excerpt now caps at 140 runes total (139 + ellipsis).

user_story: As the webview I page summaries by keyset.
expected: next_cursor is returned and passing cursor= yields the next page without duplicates or skipped rows.

user_story: As a client I choose whether conflicts are listed.
expected: Conflict notes are excluded by default and included with include_conflicts=1.

user_story: As a client I can scope /notes.
expected: parent_id, tag_id and query (with summary=1) filter the list; query uses the FTS index.

user_story: As a clipper I create a note with minimum fields.
expected: POST /notes fills id, created/updated/user times, markup_language=1, type_=1 and returns the note.
fix: internal/clipper/notes.go: POST /notes response now sets type_=1.

user_story: As a clipper I attach tags at creation.
expected: tag_ids attaches existing tags; an unknown tag returns 400 and no note is created.
evidence: qa/test_api.py — create with tags rejects unknowns

user_story: As a clipper I can send HTML instead of Markdown.
expected: body_html on POST /notes is converted to Markdown (Joplin Data API behavior).

user_story: As a client I get a clean miss.
expected: GET /notes/<missing> returns 404 {'error':'not found'}.

user_story: As a clipper I update note fields.
expected: PUT accepts title, body, parent_id, is_todo, todo_completed, todo_due, source_url, author, markup_language, order and returns the stamped note.

user_story: As a clipper I can update from HTML.
expected: PUT body_html replaces the body with converted Markdown; empty HTML leaves the body alone.

user_story: As a client I cannot update a missing note.
expected: PUT /notes/<missing> returns 404 before any policy or JSON work.

user_story: As a clipper I remove a note.
expected: DELETE /notes/{id} returns {'status':'ok'}, the note is gone, and the deletion is queued for sync.

user_story: As a client I manage notebooks.
expected: GET/POST/GET id/PUT/DELETE /folders create, rename, re-parent and delete folders with 404s for misses.

user_story: As a client I fetch the notebook tree.
expected: GET /folders?as_tree=1 returns folders with nested children arrays.

user_story: As a client I list a notebook's notes.
expected: GET /folders/{id}/notes supports limit/page/order/fields/include_conflicts and summary mode.

user_story: As a client I manage tags.
expected: GET/POST/GET id/PUT/DELETE /tags work with 404s for misses.

user_story: As a clipper I tag a note.
expected: POST /tags/{id}/notes {'id': noteId} links them; repeating is idempotent.

user_story: As a clipper I untag a note.
expected: DELETE /tags/{id}/notes/{noteId} removes the link and queues the link deletion.

user_story: As a client I list a note's tags.
expected: GET /notes/{id}/tags returns full tag entities with pagination and fields support.
evidence: qa/test_api.py — note tags pagination and fields

user_story: As a client I list notes for a tag.
expected: GET /tags/{id}/notes returns tagged notes with paging/fields, and summary mode when asked.

user_story: As a client I search note text.
expected: GET /search?query= matches titles and bodies via FTS5; type defaults to note.

user_story: As a client I search notebook names.
expected: type=folder matches a folder-title prefix case-insensitively.

user_story: As a client I search tag names.
expected: type=tag matches a tag-title prefix case-insensitively.

user_story: As a client I get a clear error for no query.
expected: query is required (400); a query with no matches returns an empty items list, not an error.

user_story: As a client FTS syntax in a query cannot break the server.
expected: Quotes, *, parentheses and colons are handled without 500s and still return sensible matches.

user_story: As a clipper I upload an attachment.
expected: POST /resources multipart (data + optional props/title) stores metadata and bytes; GET /resources/{id}/file returns them with type/filename.

user_story: As a client I update or delete a resource.
expected: PUT changes title/filename/mime; DELETE removes metadata and queues the deletion.

user_story: As an operator the read-only policy also covers attachments.
expected: With no writable folders, POST/PUT/DELETE /resources are refused like note mutations.

user_story: As a client I can read note history.
expected: GET /revisions lists raw revision metadata, GET /{id} returns one or 404, DELETE removes it.

user_story: As a client I can poll the change feed.
expected: GET /events?cursor= returns item changes with has_more; GET /events/{id} returns one or 404.

user_story: As the desktop page I can call the API cross-origin.
expected: Preflight from app://localhost is allowed for GET/POST/PUT/DELETE with Content-Type/Authorization.

user_story: As a client malformed input is rejected cleanly.
expected: POST/PUT with invalid JSON return 400 'invalid JSON: …' and change nothing.

user_story: As an operator I can run the server read-only.
expected: With an empty allow-list, creating notes/folders/tags and mutating notes returns 403 with a configuration hint.

user_story: As an operator I can allow specific notebooks/tags.
expected: By title or ID, only allow-listed folders accept note creates/updates and only allow-listed tags can be attached.

user_story: As an operator bad parent IDs are refused.
expected: Creating or moving a note into a nonexistent folder returns 400 instead of storing an orphan.

user_story: As a user international text survives the API.
expected: Emoji, CJK, combining marks and multi-KB bodies round-trip byte-identically through create/get/update.

user_story: As a client bad requests fail predictably.
expected: Unknown paths return 404; unsupported methods return 405 (or chi's method response), never a panic.

user_story: As a user note history is immutable through the API.
expected: PUT /revisions/{id} is rejected (405/400) and never rewrites stored history; missing ids 404.

user_story: As a user changes made elsewhere arrive here.
expected: PullChanges applies remote creates/updates/deletes from the delta cursor into the local store.

user_story: As a user my local changes reach the target.
expected: PushChanges uploads dirty notes, folders, tags, note-tags and resources, then stamps per-item sync times.

user_story: As a user deleting here deletes there.
expected: Deletions queued in deleted_items are sent to the target and removed from the queue.

user_story: As a user a remote delete removes a clean local note.
expected: A note with no local changes is deleted locally when the target reports it gone.

user_story: As a user simultaneous edits never lose data.
expected: The local version is kept as a new conflict note (is_conflict=1, original id set) and the remote stays canonical.

user_story: As a user a remote delete does not discard my edits.
expected: The modified local note is first kept as a conflict copy, then the original is deleted.

user_story: As a user losing a notebook does not orphan notes.
expected: Notes in a remotely deleted folder are marked is_conflict rather than silently orphaned.

user_story: As a user two edited attachments keep both.
expected: The local blob is duplicated with a new id and an 'Attachment conflict' note is filed in 'Conflicts (attachments)'.

user_story: As a user a remotely changed attachment does not clobber unsynced bytes.
expected: An unpushed local blob is copied to a conflict resource before the remote blob becomes canonical.

user_story: As a user two clients do not sync at once.
expected: A lock is acquired before a pass and released after it, with a 3-minute TTL on file targets.

user_story: As a user a locked target refuses my sync.
expected: A held exclusive lock makes the pass fail with 'sync refused' instead of proceeding unlocked.

user_story: As a user long syncs keep their lock.
expected: The held lock is refreshed every 60 s; an expired lock stops the refresh and fails.

user_story: As a user I cannot sync with a newer format.
expected: info.json version > 3 or appMinVersion > 3.7.0 refuses the sync with ErrSyncTargetUnsupported.

user_story: As a user E2EE keys from other clients are learned.
expected: Master keys in info.json are stored locally; active_master_key_id is recorded.

user_story: As a user I can read E2EE notes from Joplin.
expected: Pulled encrypted notes/resources are decrypted with the master password and stored as plaintext plus raw.

user_story: As a user my pushed notes stay encrypted on the target.
expected: When a master key is active, pushed items are encrypted (JED01 envelope) with the active key.

user_story: As a user each target tracks what it has seen.
expected: Per-item, per-target sync times advance only after a successful push, so redelivery does not echo.
fix: store/sync_state.go: ApplyPulledItem records the pulled revision's updated_time as the sync point (not wall clock), so an edit in the same millisecond can no longer be skipped; fixes a flaky local-folder rehearsal (~15% -> 0/40).

user_story: As a user items the delta missed are recovered.
expected: PullMissingItems fetches master keys/items not present in the delta and prunes stale local items.

user_story: As a user concurrent triggers do not double-sync.
expected: A trigger during a running pass is ignored (try-lock), never queued into a second overlapping pass.
fix: Added internal/sync/engine_coalesce_test.go: a pass held in the backend refuses an overlapping Sync (try-lock, one lock acquisition) and the buffered trigger channel keeps only one pending signal.

user_story: As a user a local folder target proves the engine end to end.
expected: Two profiles syncing through a folder converge: edits, tags, deletes and conflicts match Joplin semantics.

user_story: As a Dropbox user I can sync through my own app folder.
expected: OAuth token refresh, upload/download/delta/children, locks and path mapping work against the API.

user_story: As a Dropbox user I can authorize without copying a token.
expected: PKCE authorization-code flow on a loopback redirect stores and refreshes dropbox_token.json.

user_story: As a Joplin Server user I can sync with my server.
expected: Session auth, /api/items paths and server locks work against a real Joplin Server.
evidence: qa/joplin-server-e2e.sh against a real Joplin Server 3.x (Docker, SQLite): vault A pushes a notebook and note, a fresh vault B pulls the same title/body, and the E2EE leg seeds a master key, checks the server-side item is an encrypted envelope with no plaintext, decrypts it in vault B, and keeps it unreadable without the password
fix: internal/sync/client.go: Get reports a typed ErrNotFound, and syncinfo treats it as a missing info.json so a fresh Joplin Server target can push its first one without letting item/blob fetches overwrite local data; qa/joplin-server-e2e.sh now runs plaintext and E2EE round trips and checks the server-side envelope.

user_story: As an operator S3 is opt-in at build time.
expected: The default binary's S3 backend is a stub with an explanatory error; -tags s3 links the real backend.
evidence: qa/s3-e2e.sh against RustFS (S3-compatible) in Docker: the default build refuses the target with the stub's message, and the `-tags s3` binary round-trips a note plaintext and E2EE (the bucket holds only envelopes, a vault with the master password decrypts, one without it never reads the body)
fix: internal/s3/client.go: isNotFound only matched the modeled NotFound type, so a missing key (AWS, MinIO and RustFS all answer NoSuchKey) aborted the first sync to a fresh bucket; it now matches the NoSuchKey/NotFound codes and a bare 404, while NoSuchBucket stays a configuration error. qa/s3-e2e.sh runs the whole path against RustFS in Docker.

user_story: As a user Joplin items round-trip losslessly.
expected: Every golden fixture deserializes and re-serializes byte-identically.

user_story: As a user metadata from newer Joplin versions survives.
expected: Unknown keys keep their exact text and position through the raw passthrough.

user_story: As a client metadata values have the right JSON types.
expected: Numeric/boolean known keys are emitted typed; other values stay strings.

user_story: As a user my bytes are kept next to the typed row.
expected: item_raw stores the exact serialized item and is pushed verbatim until the item changes.

user_story: As a new user the database is created correctly.
expected: Opening an empty directory migrates to schema 49 and enables WAL.

user_story: As a user I can open a real Joplin profile.
expected: A Joplin-like database is migrated additively (sidecar tables only), leaving core tables intact.

user_story: As a user search reflects edits immediately.
expected: Create/update/delete keeps jl_notes_fts in sync so search never returns deleted or stale text.

user_story: As a client settings persist.
expected: GetSetting/SetSetting round-trip values in the database.
fix: Added store/settings_test.go: GetSetting/SetSetting round-trip (empty and unicode values, overwrite, no duplicate row) and survive a database reopen.

user_story: As the UI I can list conflicts.
expected: ListConflictNotes returns only is_conflict=1 notes, newest first.

user_story: As a client revisions survive restart.
expected: UpsertRevision/ListRevisions/CountRevisions/DeleteRevision persist index rows and raw metadata.

user_story: As a user attachments live on disk.
expected: SaveResourceFile/GetResourceFile round-trip bytes under the resources directory.

user_story: As a user deletions reach every target that saw the item.
expected: recordDeletion inserts one row per target only for items that were actually synced.

user_story: As a client the change feed is append-only.
expected: Each note/folder/tag mutation appends an item_changes row, and reads page by cursor.
fix: Added store/events_test.go: item_changes pages strictly after a cursor with correct has_more, no duplicates, ordered ids, single-event lookup and resumability after new mutations.

user_story: As an operator I can discover commands.
expected: gojoplin --help lists serve, sync, config, dropbox-auth and clip with short descriptions.

user_story: As an operator I can inspect resolved settings safely.
expected: config prints target, URL, user, redacted secrets, data dir, listen address and observability.

user_story: As an operator serve refuses to run unprotected.
expected: Missing api.token exits with 'api token is required' and a configuration hint.

user_story: As an operator serve refuses to run without a clipper key.
expected: Missing api.key exits with 'api key is required'.

user_story: As an operator I can run serve without a remote.
expected: serve --no-sync opens the DB, starts the API and does no remote work.

user_story: As an operator the server binds and announces itself.
expected: It logs the configured address and the API token, and serves /ping.

user_story: As an operator I can sync once from cron.
expected: sync opens the DB, builds the configured backend and runs one engine pass, failing loudly.

user_story: As a script I can check the API.
expected: clip ping sends Bearer auth and prints the ping body.

user_story: As a script I can manage notes.
expected: clip notes list/get/create/delete round-trip through the HTTP API.

user_story: As a script I can list and create notebooks.
expected: clip folders list/create return the API entities.

user_story: As a script I can list tags.
expected: clip tags list returns tags from the API.

user_story: As a script I can search.
expected: clip search <query> prints matching notes.

user_story: As a Dropbox user I can run the OAuth flow from the CLI.
expected: dropbox-auth prints a URL, waits on the loopback redirect, stores the token and reports the account.
error: dropbox-auth needs an interactive OAuth redirect against Dropbox; the loopback flow is unit tested (TestDropboxOAuth_LoopbackFlow).

user_story: As an operator secrets stay out of files.
expected: ${VAR} in api.token/key/master_password and the OTLP endpoint expands from the environment.

user_story: As a Joplin user I can reuse my settings.json.
expected: Flat dotted keys map to the same Config; missing sync target defaults and observability are applied.

user_story: As an operator env overrides the file.
expected: GOJOPLIN_* overrides and CLI overrides win over the YAML values for secrets, port and data dir.

user_story: As an operator misconfiguration fails fast.
expected: Unsupported target, missing S3 bucket/URL/region, missing server URL or empty username are rejected with specific errors.

user_story: As an operator -no-sync does not demand a remote.
expected: No-sync skips sync-target validation so a local-only config loads without S3/server fields.

user_story: As a user I get a sane default location.
expected: No server.data_dir falls back to GOJOPLIN_DATA_DIR or ~/.local/share/gojoplin.

user_story: As a user the API is local by default.
expected: Default listen host is localhost (not 0.0.0.0) and port 41184; both can be overridden.

user_story: As a user a busy port is a clear error.
expected: Serve returns a socket-in-use error rather than silently choosing another port.

user_story: As an operator I can generate shell completion.
expected: the `completion` command emits a bash/zsh/fish/powershell script (cobra-generated).

user_story: As an operator I can configure OTLP tracing.
expected: observability.tracing parses and validates; when enabled the app warns that span export is not implemented (no silent no-op).
fix: The product advertised OTLP tracing while nothing exported spans. observability now defaults to disabled and Config.UnsupportedSubsystems() makes an enabled-but-unimplemented setting warn instead of silently doing nothing (cmd/serve.go, shell/backend.go).

user_story: As an operator I can configure Prometheus metrics.
expected: observability.metrics parses and validates; when enabled the app warns that no /metrics endpoint is served yet.
fix: Same fix for metrics: no /metrics endpoint exists yet, so it is off by default and warns when on.

user_story: As an operator I can configure semantic search.
expected: rag parses and validates; when enabled the app warns that embedding search is not implemented and search stays FTS.
fix: Same fix for RAG: embedding search is not implemented; enabling it warns and search stays FTS.

user_story: As an operator I can restrict exposed MCP tools.
expected: mcp.enabled_tools parses; a non-'*' value is reported as not implemented instead of silently ignored.
fix: Same fix for mcp.enabled_tools: a non-'*' value is reported as not implemented rather than silently ignored.

user_story: As a new user the example config matches real behavior.
expected: config.yaml.example disables and annotates the not-yet-implemented observability/rag/mcp-tool settings, so copying it cannot enable a silent no-op.
fix: config.yaml.example rewritten: tracing/metrics/rag disabled and annotated NOT YET IMPLEMENTED, and the unbuilt '13 MCP tools' claim removed, so copying it cannot enable a silent no-op.
